description: HELD LOCALLY since 2026-10-01. Produced by _high/_work/scratch-dea_2026_technology-data-electricity-district-heat/extract.py from the individual datasheets of the workbook (not alldata_long: its 40 Comp. hp, airsource 10 MW COP and nameplate rows (2.7/2.5) differ from the datasheet (2.8/2.6); all other 17,000 values agree). Scope: industry-relevant heat and CHP technologies only - 59 datasheets: 01 coal extraction CHP, 04/05 gas turbines (simple cycle with heat recovery, combined cycle), 06 gas engines, 08 waste-to-energy CHP and HOP, 09 biomass CHP (back-pressure and extraction) and HOP, 10 Stirling gasified biomass, 11 SOFC and 12 PEM fuel-cell CHP, 20 onshore wind (utility; for the wind-turbine gap), 22 commercial/industrial rooftop PV+BESS (for the photovoltaic-array_battery-storage gap), 40 compression heat pumps, 41 electric boilers, 44 gas and 47 oil DH boilers, 45 geothermal DH with heat pump, 46 solar DH, 50-52 peak plants. Skipped: 02 life-time extension and 03 coal-to-biomass conversions (power-plant retrofits), 21 offshore wind, other 22 PV sheets, 20 domestic turbines, 23 wave. Base year: 2025 where the sheet prints a 2025 central value (20, 22, 40, 41, 45, 47), else 2020 (all other sheets; no 2025 column). Lower/upper loaded as value-min/max only when printed for the same year: 2020 sheets have 2020 ranges; the 2025 sheets 40/41/45/47 print ranges only for 2030 and 2050, so they have no range; 20 onshore prints ranges for 2020 only. Ranges equal to the central value are dropped. All other years go to _projections.csv (the DEA convention in this folder). Loaded: capacity (MW_e electric-output for CHP and power; MW_h thermal-output for heat-only), net annual-average electrical and heat efficiency (target electricity/heat for CHP; blank target for heat-only, = COP for heat pumps), name-plate efficiency only where no annual average is printed (01 coal, 10 Stirling), lifetime, construction time, minimum load, availability/capacity factor/degradation where printed, CH4 and N2O per GJ fuel input (CO2 is not printed), capex = Nominal investment (*total) per MW (M EUR/MW x1000 to EUR/kW), fixed O&M (EUR/MW/y /1000 to EUR/kW-yr), variable O&M per MWh output (for heat-only sheets with a split, the 'other O&M' row, i.e. excluding the auxiliary electricity cost). Derived: heat-to-power-ratio = 1/Cb (Cb printed; back-pressure mode); efficiency-chp = electrical + heat annual average for back-pressure CHP (report note H: total efficiency is their sum); PV capacity factor = AC full-load hours/8760; temperature-output from the DH forward temperature in the sheet title (40, 45 and large 08/09 sheets). Flows: auxiliary electricity per GJ heat for heat-only boilers and solar DH (not included in their efficiency, guideline p.23); for heat pumps and geothermal it is inside the COP (notes D/M) and goes to _other-values. _other-values: name-plate efficiencies, equipment/installation splits, per-MW-input and per-tonne-input costs of biomass/WtE CHP (note J: not additive to the per-MW_e cost), outages, Cb/Cv, condensate, fuel-storage cost, start-up costs, geothermal well and heat-pump split, PV/battery details. Not extracted: SO2/NOx/particles (non-GHG), regulation and start-up times, space requirement, binary design flags, per-DC PV rows. Locators: 'report p.N' is the PDF page, which equals the table-of-contents page numbers (pages carry no printed number); the 11 SOFC and 12 PEMFC chapters are not in the v0019 report (datasheets only). All efficiencies of thermal plants are on LHV (guideline p.22); emissions per GJ fuel at LHV (p.25). COST BASIS overnight = EPC/overnight price incl. on-site infrastructure, excluding owners' costs and interest during construction (guideline p.25-26); onshore wind is total-plant (includes land, neighbour settlements, decommissioning of old turbines and construction loan interest, note H).

description: HELD LOCALLY since 2026-10-01. Locators are printed page numbers (PDF page = printed + 8; front matter in roman numerals). An ENERGY STAR measure catalogue; almost every number is reprinted from other sources (Hackensellner 2000, Weinzierl et al. 2000, Seldeslachts 1999, NOVEM, CADDET, EIA 1997...), named at the end of each note. All costs: price year not stated, publication year 2003 used; underlying sources date 1993-2001. Heating value: HHV per footnote 4 for kBtu values; the Brand mash-filter saving is explicitly LHV.

author: Worrell, E., Kermeli, K. and Galitsky, C.
title: Energy Efficiency Improvement and Cost Saving Opportunities for Cement Making: An ENERGY STAR Guide for Energy and Plant Managers
description: HELD LOCALLY since 2026-10-01. Locators are printed page numbers (PDF page = printed + 5; front matter in roman numerals). An ENERGY STAR measure catalogue: nearly every number is reprinted from other sources (ECRA 2009, Hollingshead and Venta 2009, Cembureau 1997, Holderbank 1993...), named at the end of each note. The guide writes ton = short ton and tonne = metric ton; per-ton values are converted to per tonne with an explicit formula (MBtu/ton x 1.055056/0.907185 = GJ/t; kWh/ton / 0.907185), printed metric values are used where the guide prints them. Main file: Table 2 2009 U.S. baseline (kiln feed preparation per t raw material, wet and dry clinker production fuel (HHV) and electricity per t clinker, finish grinding per t cement) with calcination CO2 0.51 t/t clinker; raw-material crushers and mills (incl. TXI plant before/after); coal mills (Cembureau, MPS by fuel); kiln types (wet, long dry, 3-6 stage preheater from Table 1, precalciner, best precalciner); clinker coolers (efficiency, conversion capex); waste-heat power (steam Rankine, ORC, Kalina capex; Indian 8 MW plant); finish mills (ball, VRM, ring roller, Horomill, HPGR, combined circuits, Table 5 configurations); advanced technologies (fluidized bed kiln, geopolymer, belite clinker, Aether). Flows: raw meal per t clinker, clinker per t cement (USGS 2008 conversion factors), electricity output of waste-heat power per t clinker (per short ton, unconverted). _measures.csv: every row of Tables 8 (dry) and 9 (wet), savings per short ton cement as printed (one row per fuel/electricity saving), payback as printed, investment cost from the Sect. 6 text added to the first row of each measure. _other-values.csv: Table 2 primary energy, totals and carbon columns, sector statistics, alternative ranges, Table 5 HPGR shares, Table 7 kiln-feed substitutes, percentages for advanced technologies. Not loaded: plant-wide cross-cutting measure details (motors, compressed air, fans, lighting; only their Table 8/9 rows), energy-management text, figures 1-10 (charts only), NOx values, and costs without a technology. All costs: price year not stated, publication year 2013 used; most cost figures come from 1993-2010 sources.
